questions.question: 80062. A number when divided by 432 leaves a remainder of 77. If the same number is divided by 16, what will be the remainder?
questions.explain:
Question: A number when divided by 432 leaves a remainder of 77. If the same number is divided by 16, what will be the remainder?

Solution:
ধরি,
সংখ্যাটি N

প্রশ্নানুসারে,
N = 432q + 77

এখন, 432 = 16 × 27 এবং 77 = 16 × 4 + 13

সুতরাং,
N = 16 × 27q + 16 × 4 + 13
= 16(27q + 4) + 13

অতএব, সংখ্যাটিকে 16 দিয়ে ভাগ করলে ভাগশেষ হবে 13

questions.question: 80061. Correct about striae of Retzius -
questions.option2: Darker area having more inorganic content
questions.option3: First forms over the dential cups or incisal area
questions.explain:
Striae of Retzius are incremental growth lines of enamel that reflect the rhythmic deposition of enamel during amelogenesis.
They are found in enamel, not dentin.
They represent periodic variations in enamel mineralization.
The first-formed enamel near the cusp tips and incisal edges shows the earliest incremental markings.
They extend from the DEJ toward the enamel surface.

questions.question: 80060. Which defensive reaction commonly develops beneath a dead tract?
questions.explain:
A dead tract is an area of dentinal tubules containing empty tubules due to the death or withdrawal of odontoblastic processes, commonly associated with caries or irritation.
As a defensive response to pulpal irritation, odontoblasts or odontoblast-like cells can deposit tertiary (reparative) dentin along the pulpal wall beneath the affected area.

questions.question: 80059. Which periodontal ligament (PDL) fiber group primarily resists vertical intrusive forces?
questions.explain:
The oblique fibers of the periodontal ligament are the most numerous and important fibers for resisting vertical (intrusive) occlusal forces.
They run from the cementum in an oblique direction coronally toward the alveolar bone. When an intrusive force is applied, these fibers become tensioned and help convert the compressive force into tension, thereby supporting the tooth within its socket.

questions.question: 80058. Taurodontism is best described as:
questions.option1: An extra root on a molar
questions.option2: Enlarged pulp chamber with apically displaced root furcation
questions.explain: Taurodontism ("bull tooth") features an enlarged, elongated pulp chamber. The root furcation is displaced further toward the apex than normal. The resulting shape resembles ungulate teeth and significantly changes root canal anatomy.

questions.question: 80057. The cingulum is best described as:
questions.option1: A depression on the lingual surface of posterior teeth
questions.option2: A convex elevation on the lingual surface of anterior teeth
questions.option3: A ridge on the buccal surface of molars
questions.explain: The cingulum is a convex, rounded elevation occupying the cervical third of the lingual surface of anterior teeth (incisors and canine)

questions.question: 80056. Shovel-shaped incisors are most commonly found in:
questions.explain:
Shovel-shaped incisors have prominent marginal ridges and a relatively deep lingual fossa, giving the lingual surface a shovel-like appearance.
They are most characteristically seen in the maxillary central incisors, particularly in certain Asian and Native American populations

questions.question: 80055. Enamel pearls are commonly found
questions.option3: Near the furcation of mandibular first molar
questions.option4: Near the furacation of maxillary 1st premolar
questions.explain:
Enamel pearls (enamel droplets) are localized, ectopic deposits of enamel found on the root surface, most commonly in the furcation areas of molars.
They are formed when Hertwig's epithelial root sheath (HERS) retains ameloblastic potential and produces enamel on the root surface.
They are particularly common in the furcation region of mandibular molars.
Clinically, enamel pearls can interfere with periodontal attachment and may contribute to localized periodontal problems because connective tissue cannot attach normally to enamel.

questions.question: 80054. Which one is correct?
questions.option2: Main type of collagen is Type III
questions.explain:
Pulp is endoderm in origin  — Dental pulp develops from the ectomesenchyme of the dental papilla, which is derived from neural crest cells.

Main type of collagen is Type III  — Type I collagen is the predominant collagen in dental pulp.

 Pulp has elastic fibers - Normal dental pulp is generally described as lacking true elastic fibers, although elastic fibers may be associated with blood-vessel walls.

questions.question: 80053. Sharpey's fibers are embedded in all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explain:
Sharpey's fibers are the terminal portions of principal periodontal ligament fibers that become embedded in the cementum and alveolar bone proper.
They are associated with the PDL, but enamel does not contain Sharpey's fiber attachment.

questions.question: 80052. Which nerve fiber carries sharp, well-localized pain?
questions.explain:
Aδ (A-delta) fibers are small, myelinated fibers that conduct impulses rapidly and are responsible for sharp, well-localized (“fast”) pain, particularly in the pulp.
Aδ fibers → sharp, quick, well-localized pain
C fibers → dull, aching, poorly localized pain

questions.question: 80051. In which part of the tooth are the incremental lines of von Ebner found?
questions.explain:
The incremental lines of von Ebner are found in dentin. They represent the daily rhythmic deposition of dentin matrix by odontoblasts. As dentin is deposited, it forms fine, parallel, hypomineralized lines that run perpendicular to the dentinal tubules. These lines are best seen in decalcified sections of dentin.

They are not found in enamel (which has Lines of Retzius), not in cementum (which has incremental lines of Salter), and not in pulp.

questions.question: 80050. The incisive foramen transmits:
questions.explain: The incisive foramen (also called the nasopalatine foramen) is located behind the maxillary central incisors and transmits the nasopalatine nerve and vessels .

questions.question: 80049. The furcation is:
questions.option1: The area between the roots of a multirooted tooth
questions.option2: The junction between crown and root
questions.explain: The furcation is the area where the roots of a multirooted tooth diverge. Furcation involvement is a common finding in periodontal disease and can complicate treatment .

questions.question: 80048. The periodontal ligament is composed primarily of:
questions.explain: The periodontal ligament is primarily composed of collagen fibers (mainly type I and III). These fibers are arranged in specific groups (alveolar crest, horizontal, oblique, apical, interradicular) that resist various forces .

questions.question: 80047. Acellular cementum:
questions.option2: Is the most recently formed cementum
questions.option4: Is thickest at the root apex
questions.explain: Acellular cementum (primary cementum) directly covers the root dentin, particularly in the cervical and middle thirds of the root. It does not contain embedded cells (cementocytes) and is formed slowly .

questions.question: 80046. The tissue that provides dentin trophic support is:
questions.explain: The dental pulp provides trophic (nutritional) support to dentin through the odontoblastic processes that extend into the dentinal tubules. The pulp also provides sensory and defensive functions .

questions.question: 80045. What does the reduced epithelium become after the tooth has erupted?
questions.explain: The reduced enamel epithelium, which covers the crown of the erupting tooth, fuses with the oral epithelium to become the junctional epithelium after eruption. This forms the epithelial attachment to the tooth .

questions.question: 80044. The epithelium which maps out the shape of the root is called:
questions.explain: Hertwig's epithelial root sheath (HERS) is the structure that maps out the shape of the root. It induces the differentiation of odontoblasts that form root dentin .

questions.question: 80043. What are enamel spindles?
questions.option1: Change of direction of enamel prisms
questions.option2: Sheet-like fault running through the full thickness of enamel
questions.option4: When dentinal tubules have extended into the enamel
questions.explain: Enamel spindles are odontoblastic processes that have extended into the enamel layer before it was fully mineralized. They appear as spindle-shaped structures near the dentinoenamel junction .

questions.question: 80042. The periodontal ligament is formed from:
questions.explain: The periodontal ligament, along with cementum and alveolar bone proper, is derived from the dental follicle (dental sac). This mesenchymal tissue surrounds the developing tooth germ .

questions.question: 80041. Which type of nerve fibers predominantly form the plexus of Raschkow?
questions.explain:
The plexus of Raschkow is formed by both myelinated A-delta fibers and unmyelinated C fibers:

· A-delta fibers — These are myelinated nerve fibers that are mainly located in the peripheral region of the plexus, close to the odontoblast layer. They are responsible for sharp, well-localized pain and are involved in dentinal sensitivity (especially the hydrodynamic theory).
· C fibers — These are unmyelinated nerve fibers found deeper in the plexus, closer to the pulp core. They respond to slow, dull, aching pain and are associated with inflammatory pulpitis.

questions.question: 80040. The most recently formed layer of dentin, unmineralized, closest to the pulp is called:
questions.explain: Predentin is the unmineralized organic matrix of dentin that is secreted by odontoblasts before mineralization. It is located closest to the pulp and represents the most recently formed dentin

questions.question: 80039. Mantle dentine is:
questions.option4: Dentine formed within the dental tubules
questions.explain: : Mantle dentin is the first layer of mineralized dentin formed, located immediately adjacent to the enamel or cementum. It is characterized by a different collagen fiber orientation than circumpulpal dentin

questions.question: 80038. Which tissue of the tooth is of ectodermal origin?
questions.explain: Enamel is unique among dental tissues in being of ectodermal origin. It is formed by ameloblasts derived from the inner enamel epithelium. Dentin, cementum, and pulp are of mesodermal (mesenchymal) origin .

questions.question: 80037. What is the name of the cells that form dentine?
questions.explain: Odontoblasts are the cells responsible for dentin formation (dentinogenesis). They line the pulp chamber and extend processes into the dentinal tubules .

questions.question: 80036. The term "succedaneous teeth" refers to:
questions.option1: Permanent teeth that replace primary teeth
questions.explain: Succedaneous teeth are permanent teeth that replace primary teeth (incisors, canines, and premolars). The permanent molars are not succedaneous because they have no primary predecessors .

questions.question: 80035. The dental formula for primary dentition is:
questions.explain:
The primary (deciduous) dentition contains 20 teeth—10 in each arch.
The dental formula per quadrant is:
Incisors (I): 2
Canine (C): 1
Premolars (P): 0
Molars (M): 2
Therefore:
I₂/₂ C₁/₁ M₂/₂ × 2 = 20 teeth

questions.question: 80034. Primary teeth begin to calcify at what stage of prenatal development?
questions.explain:
The primary teeth begin to calcify during the prenatal period, generally around the 4th month in utero.
Maxillary and mandibular primary central incisors are among the first primary teeth to begin calcification.
Calcification starts at the incisal edge/cusp tips and progresses cervically.
By birth, varying degrees of calcification have already occurred in all primary teeth.

questions.question: 80033. The total number of tooth pattern determination theories proposed for all types of dentitions is:
questions.explain:
There are two major theories of tooth pattern determination:
Field Theory – proposes that groups of cells within developmental fields determine the type, position, and morphology of developing teeth.
Clone Theory – proposes that individual tooth types arise from specific cell clones, with developmental interactions determining tooth morphology.

questions.question: 80032. During which morphological stage of tooth development does the enamel organ assume the shape of the future crown?
questions.explain:
During the bell stage, the enamel organ undergoes morphodifferentiation, where it assumes the shape and outline of the future crown.
Inner enamel epithelium (IEE) determines the shape and size of the future crown.
Cells of the IEE subsequently differentiate into ameloblasts, which form enamel.
The bell stage is therefore characterized by both morphodifferentiation and histodifferentiation.

questions.question: 80031. Total number of physiological stages of tooth development is:
questions.explain: Tooth development has two main physiological stages: the pre-eruptive stage (before eruption) and the post-eruptive stage (after eruption) .

questions.question: 80030. The cusp of Carabelli is most commonly found on:
questions.explain: The cusp of Carabelli is an accessory cusp located on the mesiolingual surface of the maxillary first molar. It is present in approximately 60% of maxillary first molars .

questions.question: 80029. Which tooth has an oblique ridge on its occlusal surface?
questions.explain:
The oblique ridge is a characteristic feature of the maxillary molars, especially the maxillary first molar.
It is formed by the union of the distal ridge of the mesiopalatal (mesiolingual) cusp with the mesial ridge of the distobuccal cusp.
It runs obliquely across the occlusal surface, from the mesiopalatal cusp toward the distobuccal cusp.

questions.question: 80028. The mandibular first molar typically has how many cusps?
questions.explain:
The mandibular first permanent molar typically has 5 cusps:
3 buccal cusps → mesiobuccal, distobuccal, distal
2 lingual cusps → mesiolingual, distolingual
It commonly has a pentagonal occlusal outline.

questions.question: 80027. The remnants of dental lamina are called as:
questions.explain:
During tooth development, the dental lamina connects the developing tooth germ with the oral epithelium. As the tooth develops, the dental lamina degenerates and breaks up, leaving epithelial remnants within the gingiva and jaw.
These remnants are called cell rests of Serres.
Cell rests of Serres → remnants of dental lamina 
Cell rests of Malassez → remnants of Hertwig's epithelial root sheath (HERS)

questions.question: 80026. Which of the following is NOT a constituent of the tooth germ?
questions.explain:
The tooth germ consists of three primary components:
Enamel organ → develops into enamel
Dental papilla → develops into dentin and dental pulp
Dental follicle (dental sac) → develops into cementum, periodontal ligament, and alveolar bone
The enamel knot is a transient signaling center within the enamel organ, especially important during tooth morphogenesis and cusp patterning. It is not considered one of the three principal components of the tooth germ.

questions.question: 80025. Which structure differentiates to form ameloblast?
questions.explain: The inner enamel epithelium (IEE) differentiates into ameloblasts, which are responsible for enamel formation. The outer enamel epithelium, stellate reticulum, and stratum intermedium serve supportive and nutritional roles during tooth development .

questions.question: 80024. Nerve fibres/receptors of the periodontal ligament are:
questions.option3: Golgi type present in the root apex
questions.explain: The periodontal ligament contains several types of mechanoreceptors and sensory nerve endings. Ruffini-like endings are particularly important mechanoreceptors in the PDL and help detect tooth movement and occlusal forces.

questions.question: 80023. Choose the correct one-
questions.option1: Main fiber of dentin is type lll
questions.option2: Circumpulpal dentain mainly of α  fibers
questions.option3: Dentin that is formed prior to tooth eruption is kown as predentin
questions.explain:
Main fiber type of dentin is type 1. Trace amount of type III & type V also found.

Circumpulpal dentain mainly of ẞ fibers.

Dentin that is formed prior to tooth eruption is kown as primary dentin.

questions.question: 80022. Which is NOT correct about the lining mucosa of the oral cavity?
questions.option2: Present in the lips, cheeks and vestibule
questions.explain:
Lining mucosa is generally non-keratinized, soft, moist, and relatively flexible/elastic. It covers the lips, labial and buccal mucosa, alveolar mucosa, soft palate, ventral surface of tongue, and floor of mouth.
Its relatively high elasticity allows movement and stretching.

questions.question: 80021. What is the decimal value of the hexadecimal number (AF)<sub>16</sub>?
questions.explain:
- Hexadecimal সংখ্যা (AF)16 এর দশমিক রূপ 175.

দেওয়া আছে, 
Hexadecimal সংখ্যা = (AF)16

Hexadecimal-এ A = 10 এবং F = 15

∴ (AF)16 ​= A × 161 + F × 160
= 10 × 16 + 15 × 1 
= 160 + 15 
= 175
সুতরাং, (AF)16​ = (175)10​​

questions.question: 80020. Which of the following file formats is mainly used for storing digital audio?
questions.explain:
- WAV file formats is mainly used for storing digital audio.

- WAV একটি অডিও ফাইল ফরম্যাট, যা মূলত ডিজিটাল শব্দ (audio) সংরক্ষণের জন্য ব্যবহৃত হয়।
- WAV-এর পূর্ণরূপ: Waveform Audio File Format.
- এটি সাধারণত আনকমপ্রেসড, তাই শব্দের মান খুব ভালো, তবে ফাইলের আকার বড়।

• অন্যান্য audio file formats:
- আনকমপ্রেসড: WAV, AIFF
- লসলেস কমপ্রেসড: FLAC, ALAC
- লসি কমপ্রেসড: MP3, AAC, OGG

• অপরদিকে, JPEG, PNG, GIF ও TIFF সবই ইমেজ (ছবি) ফরম্যাট।
- JPEG লসি কমপ্রেশনে ছবি রাখে।
- PNG স্বচ্ছ ব্যাকগ্রাউন্ড সমর্থন করে। 
- GIF অ্যানিমেশনযুক্ত সরল ছবির জন্য ব্যবহৃত হয়। 
- TIFF উচ্চমানের ছবির জন্য ব্যবহৃত হয়।

questions.question: 80019. Which logic gate can be used alone to implement all other basic logic gates?
questions.explain:
- The NAND gate can be used alone to implement all other basic logic gates. NAND gate is called universal gate.

• লজিক গেট:
- এটি এমন একটি ইলেকট্রনিক সার্কিট যা যৌক্তিক সিদ্ধান্ত নেয়।
- এর কার্যকারিতা নির্ভর করে Boolean Algebra এর উপর, যেখানে 'সত্য' (True) কে ১ এবং 'মিথ্যা' (False) কে ০ দ্বারা বোঝানো হয়।
 
• মৌলিক লজিক গেট (Basic Logic Gates):
- AND গেট: সমস্ত ইনপুট ১ হলে আউটপুট ১ হয়, অন্যথায় ০।
- OR গেট: যেকোনো একটি ইনপুট ১ হলে আউটপুট ১ হয়, সব ০ হলে ০।
- NOT গেট: ইনপুটকে উল্টে দেয় (০ হলে ১, ১ হলে ০)।
 
• সার্বজনীন লজিক গেট (Universal Logic Gates):
- NAND গেট: AND গেট ও NOT গেটের সমন্বয়ে গঠিত, যা দিয়ে অন্যান্য সব গেট তৈরি করা যায়।
- NOR গেট: OR গেট ও NOT গেটের সমন্বয়ে গঠিত, যা দিয়েও অন্যান্য সব গেট তৈরি করা যায়।
 
• অন্যান্য গেট:
- XOR (Exclusive OR) গেট: দুটি ইনপুট ভিন্ন হলে ১, একই হলে ০ আউটপুট দেয়।
- XNOR (Exclusive NOR) গেট: দুটি ইনপুট একই হলে ১, ভিন্ন হলে ০ আউটপুট দেয়।

questions.question: 80018. Fifth-generation computers are based on-
questions.explain:
- Fifth-generation computers are based on Artificial Intelligence.

- কম্পিউটারের বিবর্তন বা প্রজন্ম (Generation) মূলত ব্যবহৃত প্রযুক্তির ওপর ভিত্তি করে ৫টি ভাগে বিভক্ত, যেখানে প্রতিটি ধাপে আকার ছোট, গতি বৃদ্ধি এবং কার্যক্ষমতা বেড়েছে।

প্রথম প্রজন্ম:
১। ভ্যাকুয়াম টিউব (Vacuum Tubes) ব্যবহার করা হতো।
২। কম্পিউটারগুলো আকারে বিশাল (ঘর সমপরিমাণ) এবং গতি খুবই ধীর।
৩। প্রচুর তাপ উৎপন্ন হতো এবং প্রচুর বিদ্যুৎ খরচ হতো।
৪। যান্ত্রিক ভাষা (Machine Language) এবং ম্যাগনেটিক ড্রাম মেমরি ব্যবহৃত হতো।
 
দ্বিতীয় প্রজন্ম:
১। ভ্যাকুয়াম টিউবের পরিবর্তে ট্রানজিস্টর (Transistors) ব্যবহার।
২। ১ম প্রজন্মের তুলনায় আকারে ছোট, দ্রুত এবং বেশি নির্ভরযোগ্য।
৩। অ্যাসেম্বলি ভাষা (Assembly Language) এবং উচ্চতর ভাষা (FORTRAN, COBOL) এর ব্যবহার শুরু।
৪। ম্যাগনেটিক কোর মেমরি ব্যবহৃত হতো। 

 তৃতীয় প্রজন্ম:
১। ট্রানজিস্টরের পরিবর্তে সমন্বিত সার্কিট বা আইসি (Integrated Circuits - IC) ব্যবহার।
২। পূর্বের চেয়ে অনেক ছোট, দ্রুত এবং বিদ্যুৎ খরচ কম।
৩। কিবোর্ড এবং মনিটরের ব্যবহার শুরু।
৪। ব্যাচ প্রসেসিংয়ের পরিবর্তে রিয়েল-টাইম অপারেটিং সিস্টেম চালু। 

চতুর্থ প্রজন্ম (১৯৭১-বর্তমান):
১। মাইক্রোপ্রসেসর (Microprocessors) ব্যবহার, যেখানে হাজার হাজার আইসি একটি চিপে থাকে।
২। অতি ক্ষুদ্র (PC, ল্যাপটপ), অত্যন্ত দ্রুত এবং শক্তিশালী।
৩। সাধারণ মানুষের ব্যবহারের উপযোগী এবং ইন্টারনেট প্রযুক্তির বিকাশ।
৪। সেমিকন্ডাক্টর মেমরি (RAM, ROM) প্রযুক্তির ব্যবহার। 

পঞ্চম প্রজন্ম (বর্তমান ও ভবিষ্যৎ):
১। কৃত্রিম বুদ্ধিমত্তা (Artificial Intelligence - AI) এবং অতি বৃহৎ স্কেল ইন্টিগ্রেশন (UVLSI)।
২। মানুষের মতো চিন্তা করার ক্ষমতা, ভয়েস রিকগনিশন, এবং প্রাকৃতিক ভাষা বোঝার ক্ষমতা।
৩। অকল্পনীয় দ্রুতগতি এবং সমান্তরাল প্রসেসিং (Parallel Processing)। উদাহরণ: রোবোটিক্স, কোয়ান্টাম কম্পিউটার।

questions.question: 80017. Which of the following devices converts digital signals into suitable signals for transmission and also converts received signals back into digital form?
questions.explain:
-  Modem converts digital signals into suitable signals for transmission and also converts received signals back into digital form.

• মডেম (Modem):
- মডেম শব্দটি Modulator ও Demodulator শব্দের সংক্ষিপ্ত রূপ।

- মডুলেশনে ডিজিটাল সংকেত অ্যানালগ (Analog) সংকেতে রূপান্তর হয় এবং ডিমডুলেটর অ্যানালগ সংকেত ডিজিটাল সংকেতে রূপান্তর হয়।

questions.question: 80016. A car travels 60 miles from Town A to Town B at 30 mph, and returns along the same route at 60 mph. What is the average speed of the car for the entire round trip?
questions.explain:
Question: A car travels 60 miles from Town A to Town B at 30 mph, and returns along the same route at 60 mph. What is the average speed of the car for the entire round trip?

Solution:
আমরা জানি, 
সমান দূরত্বের জন্য গড় গতি = 2ab/(a + b)
এখানে,
a = 30 mph
b = 60 mph

গড় গতি = (2 × 30 × 60)/(30 + 60)
= 3600/90
= 40

∴ পুরো যাত্রাপথে গাড়ির গড় গতি = 40 mph

questions.question: 80015. A man can row at 15 km/hr in still water. It takes him twice as long to row a certain distance upstream as to row the same distance downstream. Find the rate of the stream.
questions.explain:
Question: A man can row at 15 km/hr in still water. It takes him twice as long to row a certain distance upstream as to row the same distance downstream. Find the rate of the stream.

Solution:
Let,
Speed of the stream = x km/hr

Then,
Upstream speed = (15 - x) km/hr
Downstream speed = (15 + x) km/hr

Let the equal distance in both cases = d km.

According to the question,
Upstream time = 2 × Downstream time

Therefore,
d/(15 - x) = 2d/(15 + x)
⇒ 1/(15 - x) = 2/(15 + x)
⇒ 15 + x = 2(15 - x)
⇒ 15 + x = 30 - 2x
⇒ x + 2x = 30 - 15
⇒ 3x = 15
⇒ x = 15/3
⇒ x = 5

∴ Speed of the stream = 5 km/hr

questions.question: 80014. A metro rail train 180 meters long running at 54 km/hr completely passes a jogger running on an adjacent pathway in the same direction in 18 seconds, assuming the jogger's length is negligible. What is the running speed of the jogger in km/hr?
questions.explain:
Question: A metro rail train 180 meters long running at 54 km/hr completely passes a jogger running on an adjacent pathway in the same direction in 18 seconds, assuming the jogger's length is negligible. What is the running speed of the jogger in km/hr?

Solution:
Here,
Length of the metro rail train = 180 meters
Speed of the train = 54 km/hr
Time taken to pass the jogger = 18 seconds
Since the jogger's length is negligible, the distance to be covered is equal to the length of the train = 180 meters.

Let,
The running speed of the jogger = v km/hr (since the train overtakes the jogger, 54 > v)

We know that,
When two objects move in the same direction, Relative Speed = Difference of their individual speeds

Therefore,
Relative speed in the same direction = (54 - v) km/hr
Relative speed in m/s = (54 - v) × (5/18) m/s [1 km/hr = 5/18 m/s]

Also, Relative speed = Distance/Time
= 180/18
= 10 m/s

According to the question:
(54 - v) × (5/18) = 10
⇒ 54 - v = 10 × (18/5)
⇒ 54 - v = 2 × 18
⇒ 54 - v = 36
⇒ v = 54 - 36
⇒ v = 18

Therefore, the running speed of the jogger is 18 km/hr.

questions.question: 80013. Two water pumps running together can fill an overhead community tank in 6 hours. If Pump M running alone takes 10 hours to fill the tank, how many hours would Pump N alone take to fill the empty tank?
questions.explain:
Question: Two water pumps running together can fill an overhead community tank in 6 hours. If Pump M running alone takes 10 hours to fill the tank, how many hours would Pump N alone take to fill the empty tank?

Solution:
এখানে,
পাম্প M এবং N একত্রে সম্পূর্ণ ট্যাংকটি পূর্ণ করে = 6 ঘণ্টায়
পাম্প M একা সম্পূর্ণ ট্যাংকটি পূর্ণ করে = 10 ঘণ্টায়

সুতরাং,
পাম্প M এবং N একত্রে 1 ঘণ্টায় পূর্ণ করে = 1/6 অংশ
পাম্প M একা 1 ঘণ্টায় পূর্ণ করে = 1/10 অংশ

তাহলে,
পাম্প N একা 1 ঘণ্টায় পূর্ণ করে = (M ও N এর একত্রে পূর্ণকৃত অংশ) - (M এর একা পূর্ণকৃত অংশ)
= 1/6 - 1/10
= 5/30 - 3/30
= 2/30
= 1/15 অংশ

এখন,
পাম্প N একা 1/15 অংশ পূর্ণ করে = 1 ঘণ্টায়
সুতরাং, পাম্প N একা সম্পূর্ণ বা 1 অংশ পূর্ণ করে = 1 ÷ (1/15)
= 1 × 15
= 15 ঘণ্টায়

∴ পাম্প N একা সম্পূর্ণ খালি ট্যাংকটি পূর্ণ করতে 15 ঘণ্টা সময় নেবে।
